text:
Both getter specs have `no_opaque`, so they're inlined (their `$pure` becomes inline with direct field access) — good, that's not the opacity problem. But they have `ignore_abort`, meaning the prover treats these getters as potentially aborting. When I call them inside my ensures, `_SpecNoAbortCheck` must prove my spec body doesn't abort — but the getters are declared (via `ignore_abort`) as possibly-aborting, so the prover can't discharge it.

The fix: avoid the getter calls in the ensures. Since `is_equal_staking_metadata` is itself the comparison, the simplest sound ensures just restates the result against the same field accesses the function uses. But the cleanest approach — given the getters are `no_opaque` and inline — is to access fields directly via the inlined getters won't help. 

Better: drop the ensures entirely and just remove `ignore_abort`. The function provably never aborts (only `==`/`&&`), so an empty-asserts spec passes all three phases. Let me verify that minimal form first.
